Jiangsu Dongheng International Group Co., Ltd. v. Jiangsu Provincial International High-Tech Exhibition & Trading Center Co., Ltd. — Bankruptcy Liquidation Conversion to Composition Case

【Case Summary】

For small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with hope and value for rescue, active guidance should be provided to resolve debt crises through the bankruptcy composition procedure. The application of pre-voting rules should be explored, with all creditors' opinions being solicited through a hearing procedure. After conversion into the composition procedure, the composition agreement should be promptly approved by ruling in accordance with the voting rules that have already been adopted, thereby efficiently advancing the composition procedure, facilitating the quick revival of SMEs, and achieving the objectives of stabilizing market entities and safeguarding people's livelihoods and employment.

Applicant: Jiangsu Dongheng International Group Co., Ltd.

Respondent: Jiangsu Provincial International High-Tech Exhibition & Trading Center Co., Ltd.

On February 1, 2021, the applicant, Jiangsu Dongheng International Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongheng International), filed an application with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province for bankruptcy liquidation of the respondent, Jiangsu Provincial International High-Tech Exhibition & Trading Center Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as High-Tech Company), on the grounds that the respondent was unable to pay its debts as they fell due and its assets were insufficient to cover all liabilities. Upon review, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court found that High-Tech Company was unable to pay its debts as they fell due and its assets were insufficient to cover all liabilities, which met the acceptance conditions for bankruptcy liquidation. On February 25, 2021, the court ruled to accept the bankruptcy liquidation application filed by Dongheng International against High-Tech Company, and on the same day, appointed a bankruptcy administrator.

Upon investigation, the respondent, High-Tech Company, was registered and established with the Jiangsu Provincial Administration for Market Regulation on December 19, 2001, with a registered capital of RMB 10 million. Its shareholders were the applicant, Dongheng International, Jiangsu Dongheng Group High-Tech Industry Co., Ltd., and Jiangsu Dongheng Group International Economic and Trade Business Co., Ltd., holding shares of 90%, 5%, and 5% respectively. Its business scope included undertaking domestic and international high-tech achievements and product exhibitions, related technical inspections, consulting services, etc. As an SME that provides services for domestic companies to participate in exhibitions both domestically and internationally, High-Tech Company was listed among the 11 exhibition qualification service suppliers published by the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Commerce. In recent years, the company's exhibition business operated normally with stable income, and it had successively won bids on multiple occasions to undertake the organization of key domestic and international exhibitions for the Jiangsu delegation. Before High-Tech Company entered the bankruptcy procedure, several exhibition projects were still in progress, all of which were exhibitions within the Jiangsu Trade Promotion Plan, and the majority of exhibitors had already paid the full booth fees to the organizers through High-Tech Company. Affected by the pandemic, most exhibitions had been postponed, and the company's operations fell into difficulties. If High-Tech Company were to undergo bankruptcy liquidation, exhibitors would be unable to continue participating in the exhibitions and apply for financial subsidies, the creditor recovery rate would be low, and substantial losses would be incurred.

During the proceedings, the respondent, High-Tech Company, and the majority of creditors expressed their willingness to reach a composition to maintain the company's continued operation and their readiness to bear certain risks and make concessions in terms of benefits for the sake of rescuing the company. In view of this, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court guided the bankruptcy administrator to draft a composition agreement and solicited opinions from all creditors regarding the conversion of High-Tech Company into the composition procedure and the draft composition agreement. Ultimately, all creditors agreed to the draft composition agreement and the voting rules. On August 25, 2021, High-Tech Company applied to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court for composition and submitted the draft composition agreement, requesting conversion into the composition procedure. To ensure the rights of all parties to fully express their opinions, on September 13, 2021, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court organized a hearing with High-Tech Company, its shareholders, employee representatives, and creditor representatives, fully hearing all parties' opinions on the conversion to composition.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province held, upon trial, as follows:

I. The respondent, High-Tech Company, has hope and value for rescue.

As an SME that provides services for domestic companies to participate in exhibitions both domestically and internationally, the respondent, High-Tech Company, is listed among the 11 exhibition qualification service suppliers published by the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Commerce. Due to the impact of pandemic prevention and control measures, the company's main business could not continue. In the bankruptcy procedure, the debtor and the majority of creditors expressed their desire to rescue the company and their willingness to bear certain risks and make concessions. Following the policy guidance of "scientifically identifying and legally protecting SMEs with rescue value," and taking into account the company's ability to sustain operations and the development prospects of its industry, and after fully hearing the opinions of all parties, it was comprehensively judged that High-Tech Company has hope and value for rescue.

II. Multiple settlement modes were set for creditors to choose from.

Unlike large enterprises, SMEs have relatively small capital scales, most of their main assets are encumbered with security interests, they are significantly affected by external factors in their operations, and have weak risk-resistance capabilities. When they fall into difficulties, the limited settlement assets may lead creditors to be unwilling to invest time and resources in resolving the SMEs' financial difficulties. When guiding SMEs towards composition, full consideration should be given to the characteristics of SMEs. On the basis of seeking a balance of interests between creditors and the debtor, debts should be repaid using the benefits derived from the company's revival, i.e., the company's future operating income over a period of time, so as to maintain the company's normal operations.

In this case, to accommodate the different interest claims of creditors, the draft composition agreement set out three settlement modes, incorporating all the diverse claims of creditors into the settlement plan of the composition agreement and granting creditors equal rights of choice:

1. Immediate settlement of a certain percentage of the amount of claims confirmed by the court's ruling. This mode reflects the priority of efficiency, i.e., exchanging a discount on the settlement amount for the rapid liquidation of creditors' rights. However, the precondition is that the settlement percentage is not lower than the percentage that would be obtained under the bankruptcy liquidation scenario.

2. Temporary non-settlement within three years after the conclusion of the composition procedure, followed by repayment through the company's continued operating income thereafter. The core of this mode is "trading time for space." Based on creditors' recognition of the company's future ability to sustain operations, while ensuring the maximization of creditors' interests, it also alleviates the burden on the company's continued operations, achieving a win-win situation for all parties.

3. Given the industry characteristics of the respondent, High-Tech Company, and taking into full account the needs of exhibition creditors, for those creditors willing to continue participating in exhibitions through High-Tech Company, new contracts would be signed between the creditors and the company to continue providing exhibition services.

III. Application of pre-voting rules.

The bankruptcy procedure, as a comprehensive settlement procedure, aims to clean up all existing claims and debts of the debtor company and is irreversible. In this case, the respondent, High-Tech Company, and some creditors merely expressed their willingness to reach a composition. However, there remained significant uncertainty as to whether the composition could be entered into and whether it would be successfully concluded. If the composition procedure were entered into rashly and the creditors' meeting failed to adopt the draft composition agreement, High-Tech Company would still be declared bankrupt, which would not only result in procedural waste and further consumption of procedural costs, but also severely affect the realization of creditors' interests. Exploring the application of pre-voting rules is conducive not only to comprehensively and truthfully understanding the creditors' wishes but also to helping the court evaluate the feasibility of the composition, effectively reducing the risk of procedural waste. At the same time, to ensure the rights of all parties to fully express their opinions, this case adopted a hearing procedure, fully hearing all parties' opinions on the conversion to composition. On this basis, a preliminary conclusion on the feasibility of the composition was reached, facilitating the efficient advancement of the subsequent procedure for converting from liquidation to composition.

Regarding pre-voting rules, the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law does not provide for them; they are only reflected in the extension of the validity of out-of-court restructuring agreements in the reorganization procedure as stipulated in the Minutes of the National Conference on Civil and Commercial Trial Work. Whether the pre-voting effect of the draft composition agreement can be recognized in the subsequent composition procedure is crucial for achieving the efficient rescue of distressed SMEs.

To ensure the efficient advancement of the procedure and from the perspective of reducing institutional costs, this case explored the application of pre-voting rules, soliciting opinions from all creditors on the conversion of the respondent, High-Tech Company, to the composition procedure and on the draft composition agreement. To ensure the legality and reasonableness of the procedural rules, at the time of pre-voting, the voting rules for the draft composition agreement were simultaneously put to a vote. These voting rules clearly stated that if the composition procedure was entered into and the debtor did not make any substantive changes to the content of the draft composition agreement, no further vote was required, and the pre-voting result would be considered the voting result after conversion into the composition procedure. Ultimately, given that the company had fully disclosed its situation and the content of the draft composition agreement to the creditors, and that all creditors had voted to agree to the draft composition agreement during the pre-voting, with no substantive changes made to the content of the draft composition agreement, and no creditor raised any objection thereafter, the creditors' rights to be informed, to vote, and to object were fully protected. In accordance with the adopted voting rules, the effect of the pre-voting continued, and the composition procedure was efficiently advanced.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 95 and 96(1) of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, on September 14, 2021, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court ruled to convert High-Tech Company's bankruptcy liquidation into composition. Given that all creditors had voted to agree to the draft composition agreement during the pre-voting, no substantive changes were made to the content of the draft composition agreement, and no creditor raised any objection during the seven-day objection period granted, with the creditors' rights to be informed, to vote, and to object being fully protected, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with the adopted voting rules for the draft composition agreement, on September 22, 2021, ruled to approve the composition agreement and terminated the composition procedure.

On November 3, 2021, the bankruptcy administrator of High-Tech Company submitted a report on the execution of the composition agreement, indicating that the settlement plan under the composition agreement had been fully implemented.
